flags.headline: -5.11%, book's largest mover -- notably, this happened on a day Bitcoin itself is up sharply, not down
flags.detail: MARA -5.11% to $11.23 (prev close $11.835), the single largest move in the book today. No MARA-specific news found for today's session. What stands out: Bitcoin has rallied roughly 25% in August and trades near $79,000-$80,000 as of this week (Motley Fool, Rio Times) -- so today's decline is not a BTC-price-driven move, which is unusual for a name whose entire thesis is leveraged BTC exposure. The standing structural risk (persistent GAAP losses, $850M convertible debt, no profitability independent of crypto) is unchanged regardless of today's direction; MARA's own August 6 10-Q also disclosed it sold $1.6B (23,093 BTC) of its treasury in H1 2026 to fund debt paydown and the Long Ridge acquisition, which is older news but relevant context for why the stock may be trading more on company-specific balance-sheet/dilution concerns than on the BTC price itself lately.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means MARA's financial performance is essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price -- the company has no proven ability to generate profits independent of crypto market conditions.' Today's move actually cuts against the pure BTC-derivative framing (BTC up, MARA down), which is itself worth flagging to the desk as a thesis-relevant observation.

evidence.source: The Motley Fool -- 'Up 25% in August, Is Bitcoin Now a No-Brainer Buy?'
MARA Q2 2026 Form 10-Q (via crypto.news) -- $1.63B / 23,093 BTC sold in H1 2026

flags.headline: -4.54%, 2nd-largest mover -- AEM-specific (gold itself flat today), but no single tier-1-confirmed trigger pinpointed for today's move
flags.detail: AEM -4.54% to $213.965 (prev close $224.14). Ruled out as a gold-price move: spot gold was roughly flat today (~$4,617-4,620/oz, +0.06%). AEM's own SEC Form 6-K confirms 2026 capital expenditure guidance was raised to $2.6-2.8B (from $2.2-2.4B), reflecting the Barnat open-pit redesign at Canadian Malartic (following the July 2 rock-mass-movement incident) plus newly approved Hope Bay construction; production guidance stays near the low end of 3.3-3.5M oz. Separately, multiple outlets this run cite analyst fair-value cuts and a sharp downward revision to AEM's near-term revenue-growth outlook. These are real, thesis-relevant developments, but none of the sourcing found this run cleanly dates a fresh tier-1 catalyst to today's session specifically -- the capex/Barnat items stem from the Q2 print several weeks ago and may simply be getting re-priced now. Capped AMBER rather than escalated to RED pending a clearer same-day trigger.
flags.thesis_link: Matches AEM key_risk: 'Forward PEG of 2.12 indicates the stock is priced for continued gold price strength and production growth -- any execution miss on the 4M+ oz production target or gold price weakness could trigger meaningful valuation compression.' The capex increase and Barnat-driven production ceiling are a direct, if not newly-dated, hit on this risk.

evidence.source: SEC 6-K (Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd, FY2026 update) -- capex guidance raised to $2.6-2.8B from $2.2-2.4B
